title: Embedding model aliasing and release-cadence orchestration
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We frequently add new embedding variants (quantized, different dimension, tokenizer tweaks) but lack a standardized, reversible way to introduce them without high developer toil or customer risk. Current onboarding has ad-hoc metadata, manual alias updates, and brittle rollout patterns that cause latent regressions in reranking quality or tokenization mismatches for some tenants.

Goal: Implement a first-class model aliasing + release-cadence orchestration system for embeddings that supports: deterministic aliases (stable production name -> model-version), semantic compatibility checks, automated canary traffic shifts based on quality and latency gates, scheduled deprecation with tenant notification, and per-tenant pinning. The solution should integrate with console rollouts, runtime fallback, and observability (quality and cost metrics).
acceptance_criteria: API to create/modify model aliases: POST /aliases, GET /aliases/{name}, supports mapping to one or more model versions
Semantic compatibility checks run automatically on onboarding (dims, tokenizer hash, dtype) and block model if incompatible
Canary rollout flow that shifts traffic by percentage with automated quality/latency evaluation against a stored eval set
Automatic fallback: if latency SLO or top-5 rerank DCG drops below configured threshold, traffic reverts and alert is fired
Per-tenant pinning support so enterprise customers can lock an alias to a specific model version
Dashboards and alerting for embedding drift (cosine similarity distribution, rerank NDCG), per-model p50/p95 latency and cost-per-request
A deprecation scheduler that emails customers, creates a console banner, and surfaces migration steps
Migration tooling: batch re-embedding job template + CLI helper and clear docs in Console and onboarding guide

updates: 2026-02-15 - RFC published (Confluence). Decision: use a single alias to point to one primary model version and a list of candidate versions for canary evaluation.

2026-02-18 - Chose compatibility checks: dimension match, tokenizer-hash equality, dtype/quantization family. Trade-off: stricter checks reduce regressions but slow model onboarding for experimental quantized builds.
2026-02-22 - Prototype alias DB schema merged (PR #4523). Using Postgres with JSONB for candidate metadata to keep schema flexible for future fields.

2026-02-28 - Canary controller prototype run against internal eval set (1M pairs). Early results: candidate model A reduced average cosine similarity drift by 0.6%, but p95 latency regressed by 18ms on A100. Flagged as cost/latency trade-off.
2026-03-03 - Added automated gating: require delta-NDCG >= 0.002 and p95 latency within 10% of baseline to allow traffic ramp beyond 10%.
2026-03-06 - Implemented per-tenant pinning MVP in API (backend only). Console UX scheduled in cycle 2026-W10.
2026-03-09 - QA found edge case: embeddings with identical dims but different tokenizers produce heavy downstream rerank regressions. Added tokenizer-hash strictness to compatibility checks.

2026-03-12 - Load test: alias service sustained 10k updates/hour with background canary evaluations. Observability hooks wired; creating dashboard panels for alerting thresholds. Blocker: need migration job quota in Dedicated for bulk re-embedding (raised to ENG-39810).
notes: Trade-offs considered: keep alias mapping simple (single primary + ordered candidates) vs flexible branching DAG for model family. Chosen simplicity to reduce operational surface area.
Rollout policy: default canary ramp is 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows, but auto-stop on metric regressions. Ops can override in Console.
Security: model metadata does not contain customer PII. KMS/HSM integration not required for alias metadata, but key rotation impacts stored upload tokens (tracked separately).
Operational runbook draft located in Confluence with steps for manual rollback and emergency disable of alias mapping.
Customer communication: templates created for deprecation notices and migration recommendations; product comms will review before saying at scale.
